title: Finite modules over a regular local ring have bounded projective resolutions
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension $d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Every finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] has a projective resolution of length at most $d$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00O7, proof of the first assertion (lines 26934--26938)

proof.text: Choose a finite generating set of the maximal ideal with cardinality spanFinrank, using Mathlib Submodule.FG.exists_span_finset_card_eq_spanFinrank. Regularity and the given dimension equality make this cardinality d. Its toList is a regular system of parameters, and isRegular_and_quotients_of_generators of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] makes it regular. In the non-infinite branch of [def-weil-pbc-depth], insert its length d into the supremum; in the infinite branch the inequality is automatic. Thus depth_R(R) is at least d.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00O7 (proposition-regular-finite-gl-dim), first assertion; bounded resolution conversion uses Lemma Tag 065R (lemma-projective-dimension-ext), (1)--(3).

proof.text: For a nonzero finite module M apply IsLocalRing.exists_finite_free_resolution_to_maximalCohenMacaulay from [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-free-resolution-to-mcm]. Obtain e and an exact ComposableArrows sequence S of k+3 arrows, k=d-e, with zero endpoints, penultimate object linearly equivalent to M, finite free terms at indices 2 through k+1, and finite K at index 1 which is zero or has depth d.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00O7 (proposition-regular-finite-gl-dim), first assertion; bounded resolution conversion uses Lemma Tag 065R (lemma-projective-dimension-ext), (1)--(3).

proof.text: The zero K is a zero object and hence projective. Otherwise free_of_depth_eq_ringKrullDim from [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-mcm-free] gives Module.Free R K, hence categorical Projective K by Mathlib. All other terms at indices 2 through k+1 are free by the resolution theorem, hence also projective. This argument includes k=0, when there are no other terms.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00O7 (proposition-regular-finite-gl-dim), first assertion; bounded resolution conversion uses Lemma Tag 065R (lemma-projective-dimension-ext), (1)--(3).

proof.text: The private proved helper image_shortExact turns each exact consecutive pair f,g into the short exact sequence image(f) -> middle object -> image(g), by two applications of Mathlib ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono. In resolution_of_exact_projectives, induct on j from 0 through k to bound the Mathlib Ext projective dimension of image(S.map (j+1) (j+2)) by j. At j=0 exactness after the zero left endpoint makes the first map monic, so its image is isomorphic to the projective first term. At the successor, apply Mathlib ShortComplex.ShortExact.hasProjectiveDimensionLT_X3 to the image short exact sequence, using the previous bound and projectivity of the middle term. Exactness before the zero right endpoint makes the last map epic, so its image is the penultimate object. Transport the bound across this isomorphism and the supplied linear equivalence to M. Use clause (1) of ModuleCat.hasProjectiveResolutionLE_iff_ext_vanishing from [lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-ext-characterization] to obtain the required ProjectiveResolution of length at most k.

proof.text: Retain the same bounded resolution P: every i>d also satisfies i>d-e because d-e<=d, so P has zero terms above d. This is direct unfolding of [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], with no appeal to the projective-dimension-well-defined theorem. For a subsingleton M, use Mathlib ProjectiveResolution.self M after obtaining categorical projectivity from IsZero M. Its terms above degree zero are zero, hence so are its terms above d.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteModule_hasProjectiveResolutionLE
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim R = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, Module.Finite R M →
      ModuleCat.HasProjectiveResolutionLE M d
